proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted input \(\mathfrak u\), a table \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and a represented DAG \(D\in\mathfrak D\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}sparsest\text{-}dag\text{-}family}\), \(D\) is an I-map of \(\mathcal I\), which means
\[
   \operatorname{CI}(D)\subseteq\{c:\mathcal I(c)=1\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), for every \(c\) in the set on the right all determinantal minors in the block encoding \(c\) vanish at \(p\).  In particular, every conditional independence in \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\) holds under \(p\).  This is precisely the global Markov property of \(p\) with respect to \(D\).  Since this conclusion holds for each \(D\in\mathfrak D\),
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}
 \subseteq \bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D),
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap
 \bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D)
 =\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ},
\]
where \(\mathcal M(D)\) denotes the set of laws globally Markov to \(D\).  Finally, a graph-local determinantal generator encodes a member of \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\), hence is already one of the bit-one oracle minors in \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\).  Adjoining all such graph-local generators therefore neither changes the zero set on the declared domain nor enlarges the ideal generated by the chosen literal oracle minors.  This proves all three assertions.

Put \(R_0=\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), write \(J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle\), and put \(L_0=J_{\mathcal I}:s^\infty\).  A zero reduced normal form with respect to a basis of \(K_{\mathcal I}\) is equivalent to \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\), so \(F_{D,y}\) vanishes on the real variety of \(L_0\).  This universal vanishing assertion is a first-order sentence with rational coefficients.  The cited real-closed-field transfer theorem carries it from \(\mathbb R\) to the real algebraic closure \(R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of \(\mathbb Q\).  The cited real Nullstellensatz over \(R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) then gives an integer \(k\geq1\), finitely many \(q_1,\ldots,q_a\in R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), and \(h\in L_0R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) such that
\[
 F_{D,y}^{2k}+\sum_{i=1}^a q_i^2=h.
\]
By the definition of saturation after scalar extension, membership \(h\in L_0R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) means that there are an integer \(N\geq0\) and \(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\in R_{\mathrm{alg}}[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) satisfying
\[
 s^N h=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_jf_j.
\]
Consequently the finite identity
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{2k}+\sum_{i=1}^a q_i^2\right)
   =\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_jf_j
\]
is simultaneously a real-Nullstellensatz certificate and a saturation-membership certificate.  Conversely, exact verification of this identity proves the asserted membership by reading the two displayed implications backwards.

Only finitely many real algebraic coefficients occur, so they lie in one finite real algebraic extension \(E/\mathbb Q\).  Encode \(E\) by a primitive element, its square-free minimal polynomial and an isolating interval for the selected real embedding, encode coefficients in the power basis, encode every exponent in unary, and encode every polynomial as its expanded coefficient list.  Schoolbook arithmetic and reduction modulo the minimal polynomial use a number of rational bit operations polynomial in the total expanded input length; collection of like monomials and equality of the two coefficient maps have the same property.  The isolating data certify that the chosen embedding is real.  Thus exact verification is polynomial in the total length of the expanded certificate.  This proves the narrowed lemma.  Nothing in these definitions supplies a uniform numerical bound on the smallest possible \(k,N,q_i,a_j\) or on \([E:\mathbb Q]\), so the proof makes no claim involving \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\).  First suppose that every normal form is zero.  The finite identities supplied by the narrowed certificate lemma have, for each \((D,y)\), the form
\[
 s^{N_{D,y}}\left(F_{D,y}^{2k_{D,y}}+
       \sum_iq_{D,y,i}^2\right)=\sum_j a_{D,y,j}f_j,
 \qquad J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle .
\]
Let \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  The oracle-one and normalization conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) give \(f_j(p)=0\) for every \(j\).  Strict positivity gives \(p_z>0\).  Every recorded denominator is a product of observed marginal probabilities, each of which is a nonempty sum of positive cells; hence \(B_{D,y}(p)>0\) for every \((D,y)\), and therefore \(s(p)\neq0\).  Evaluating the certificate and dividing by \(s(p)^{N_{D,y}}\) yields
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)^{2k_{D,y}}+\sum_iq_{D,y,i}(p)^2=0.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative, so \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  By the cross-signature definition and positivity of both denominators,
\[
 0=A_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)-A_{D_0,y}(p)B_{D,y}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p).
\]
This holds for every \(D,y,p\), proving soundness of the equality circuit and its common-law conclusion.

For the second branch, an integer of bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) has fewer than \(2^{B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1}\) signed possibilities.  A reduced rational coordinate therefore has fewer than \(2^{2(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) numerator--denominator descriptions.  Taking \(m\) coordinates gives fewer than
\[
 2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}
\]
descriptions, before positivity, normalization, or coprimality removes any of them.  Canonical finite enumeration consequently checks no more than this number of distinct candidates.  Exact checks of positivity, normalization, oracle-one equations, every oracle-zero sum of squares, and a failed signature decide whether a candidate belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{\Omega}\) and separates.  The enumeration returns if and only if at least one such bounded candidate exists.  For a returned candidate \(p^\dagger\), denominator positivity and \(F_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq0\) give
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger),
\]
so the two intervention vectors differ.  This is incompatible with the universal equality certified by the first branch, establishing mutual exclusivity and soundness.  The argument supplies no bounded rational candidate merely from a nonzero normal form, which is why no unconditional termination claim is made.

Write \(t=t_\star=1/3\).  Summing the unnormalised numerator first over \(s_3\) and then over \(s_4\) gives
\[
 \sum_{s_3=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_3)(1+ts_2s_3)=2(1+t^2s_1s_2),
\]
\[
 \sum_{s_4=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_4)(1-ts_2s_4)=2(1-t^2s_1s_2).
\]
Their product is \(4(1-t^4)\), independently of \((s_1,s_2)\).  Summing over the four choices of \((s_1,s_2)\) therefore gives \(16(1-t^4)=1280/81\), proving normalization.  All four factors lie in \(\{2/3,4/3\}\), so every cell is positive.  In lexicographic \((-1,+1)\) order the sixteen probabilities are
\[
 \frac1{40}(4,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,4).
\]
Thus the table is rational, sums to one, and has minimum cell \(1/40\).

The preceding two summations show \(p_\star(s_1,s_2)=1/4\), hence \(1\perp2\).  Interchanging \((s_1,s_2)\) and \((s_3,s_4)\) gives \(p_\star(s_3,s_4)=1/4\), hence \(3\perp4\).  Conditional on \((s_1,s_2)\), the numerator is a product of one function of \(s_3\) and one function of \(s_4\); hence \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\).  Conditional on \((s_3,s_4)\), it is similarly a product of one function of \(s_1\) and one function of \(s_2\); hence \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\).

For completeness, define the elementary conditional-independence minor
\[
 \Delta_{ij\mid C}(a,b,c)
 =p(a,b,c)p(c)-p(a,c)p(b,c).
\]
Direct summation of the displayed integer table gives the following nonzero witness for every one of the other twenty elementary statements.  In every row \(a=b=-1\), and all displayed coordinates of \(c\) equal \(-1\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c@{\qquad}c|c|c}
(i,j)&C&\Delta&(i,j)&C&\Delta\\ \hline
(1,2)&\{3\}&-9/1600 &(1,2)&\{4\}&9/1600\\
(1,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,3)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(1,3)&\{2,4\}&3/1600\\
(1,4)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,4)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,4)&\{3\}&3/160 &(1,4)&\{2,3\}&3/400\\
(2,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(2,3)&\{1\}&3/160\\
(2,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(2,3)&\{1,4\}&3/400\\
(2,4)&\varnothing&-3/40 &(2,4)&\{1\}&-3/160\\
(2,4)&\{3\}&-3/160 &(2,4)&\{1,3\}&-3/400\\
(3,4)&\{1\}&-9/1600 &(3,4)&\{2\}&9/1600
\end{array}
\]
The four factorizations already proved make all their minors zero, while the table makes at least one minor nonzero for each remaining statement.  Hence these are exactly the elementary conditional independences.

It remains to verify the finite graph certificate.  Every labelled four-node DAG is generated by choosing a permutation, choosing a subset of its six forward pairs, and deduplicating edge sets.  Inclusion--exclusion on the nonempty set of sources gives the recurrence
\[
 a_q=\sum_{k=1}^q(-1)^{k+1}{q\choose k}2^{k(q-k)}a_{q-k},
 \qquad a_0=1,
\]
and hence \((a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(1,1,3,25,543)\).  For each of these \(543\) edge sets, enumerate all disjoint triples of node subsets, test d-separation by active paths, and, whenever d-separation holds, test every corresponding table minor by integer cross-multiplication.  Grouping the resulting exact Boolean certificate by edge count gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
\text{edge count}&0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
\text{all DAGs}&1&12&60&152&186&108&24\\
\text{I-maps}&0&0&0&0&2&24&24
\end{array}
\]
and the two four-edge I-maps have edge sets
\[
 \{1\to3,1\to4,2\to3,2\to4\},\qquad
 \{3\to1,3\to2,4\to1,4\to2\}.
\]
This enumeration is checkable solely by the displayed integer table, finite active-path tests, and integer equalities.  As a separate lower-bound check, the determinant table shows that each of the four cross pairs \(\{1,3\},\{1,4\},\{2,3\},\{2,4\}\) is inseparable by every subset of the other two vertices.  If one of these pairs were nonadjacent in an I-map DAG, take the later vertex in a topological order; its local Markov statement given its parents would separate that pair, contradicting the corresponding nonzero minor.  Thus every I-map has at least four edges, confirming minimality independently of the count.  The two DAGs are not Markov equivalent: \(D_A\) d-separates \(1\) and \(2\), whereas \(D_B\) does not, and \(D_B\) d-separates \(3\) and \(4\), whereas \(D_A\) does not.

Both displayed DAG factorizations follow from the four proved conditional independences.  Under \(D_A\), truncation at \(s_1=+1\) and summation over \(s_2,s_4\) give
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)
 =\sum_{s_2}p_\star(s_2)p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1,s_2)
 =p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1),
\]
where the second equality uses \(1\perp2\).  Direct sign summation gives uniform one-variable marginals and
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_t}[s_1s_3]
 =\frac{t(1-t^2)}{1-t^4}=\frac{t}{1+t^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)=\frac12+\frac{t}{2(1+t^2)}=\frac{13}{20}.
\]
Under \(D_B\), node \(3\) is an unmanipulated root; deleting the factor for intervened node \(1\) and summing the remaining conditional factors gives
\[
 T_{D_B,+1}(p_\star)=p_\star(s_3=+1)=\frac12.
\]
Thus the supplied empty background set, graph family, query, and rational table pass every check in \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), and all assertions follow.

Apply the cited Teh--Sadeghi--Soo criterion to \(X=\{1\}\), \(Y=\{3\}\), and \(\mathfrak G_\star=\{D_A,D_B\}\).  Both graphs are DAGs, so their first condition holds vacuously because neither graph has an undirected edge.  In \(D_A\), node \(1\) is an ancestor of node \(3\), whereas in \(D_B\) it is not.  Thus
\[
 A_A=\{1\},\qquad A_B=\varnothing.
\]
Every chain component of a DAG is a singleton.  The parent sets of the relevant singleton disagree:
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_A}(1)=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_B}(1)=\{3,4\}.
\]
Hence alternative \(2(a)\) fails.  For alternative \(2(b)\), reweighting removes no incoming arrow in \(D_A\), and the ancestral margin of \(3\) has vertices \(\{1,2,3\}\) and arrows \(1\to3\leftarrow2\).  In \(D_B\), \(A_B=\varnothing\) and the ancestral margin of the root \(3\) is the singleton graph on \(\{3\}\).  These two reweighted graphs do not even have the same vertex set, so they are not Markov equivalent.  Therefore the sufficient graphical criterion is not satisfied.

By the four-node proposition, \(p_\star\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I_\star}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{16}\) and
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)=\frac{13}{20}\neq\frac12=T_{D_B,+1}(p_\star).
\]
Its coordinates are \(1/10\) or \(1/40\), so their reduced numerator and denominator bit lengths are at most \(6\).  From the definition of \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), using \(H\geq0\), \(d\geq1\), \(c_0\geq1\), and \(m=16\), one has \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}>6\).  Thus \(p_\star\) occurs in the bounded enumeration.  Moreover, if the relevant cross-signature belonged to \(K_{\mathcal I_\star}\), the equality-certificate argument in the sound partial procedure would force it to vanish at \(p_\star\), contrary to the displayed gap.  Its normal form is therefore nonzero, and the bounded enumeration returns a rational positive separator, possibly one preceding \(p_\star\) in canonical order.  The displayed \(p_\star\) itself is an independently replayable admissible separator.  Hence this instance lies outside the sufficient graphical test but is resolved as nonidentification by the certificate procedure, proving the claimed strictness in the stated decision-output sense.

Fix the input, its equality-branch circuit, and \(P\) as in the proposed statement.  Since \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), every cell \(P_z\) is strictly positive.  Every recorded denominator \(B_{D,y}\) is a finite product of observed marginal probabilities.  Each such marginal is a nonempty sum of positive cells, so
\[
 B_{D,y}(P)>0\qquad\text{for every }D\in\mathfrak D\text{ and }y.
\]
There are finitely many pairs \((D,y)\).  Polynomial continuity therefore gives an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(P\) on which all these denominators remain positive.  A quotient of polynomials with nonvanishing denominator is continuously differentiable, so \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\), with derivative \(J_\tau\).

Let \(e_z\in\mathbb R^m\) be the coordinate vector for cell \(z\), and set \(W_i=e_{Z_i}-P\).  The i.i.d. sampling assumption gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P W_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P(W_iW_i^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{diag}(P)-PP^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i.
\]
For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^m\), finite support permits a uniform third-order Taylor expansion at zero:
\[
 \mathbb E_P\exp\!\left(\frac{t^{\mathsf T}W_i}{\sqrt n}\right)
 =1+\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Pt}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Independence and \((1+a/n+O(n^{-3/2}))^n\to e^a\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\exp\!\left(t^{\mathsf T}\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\right)
 \longrightarrow \exp\!\left(\frac12t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Pt\right),
\]
the moment generating function of the possibly singular normal law \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P)\).  Independently, all hypotheses of the cited multivariate i.i.d. central limit theorem hold because \(W_i\) has finite support.  Therefore
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P).
\]
Also
\[
 \mathbb E_P\|\widehat p_n-P\|_2^2=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_P)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\widehat p_n\to P\) in probability.  Since \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(P\), \(\Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\to1\), and in particular the denominator event in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) has probability tending to one.

Continuous differentiability gives the deterministic expansion
\[
 \tau(P+h)=\tau(P)+J_\tau(P)h+r(h),
 \qquad \frac{\|r(h)\|}{\|h\|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The second-moment display implies \(\sqrt n\|\widehat p_n-P\|=O_P(1)\), whence \(\sqrt n\,r(\widehat p_n-P)=o_P(1)\).  This is also the remainder conclusion of the cited multivariate delta method.  The off-event definition changes the estimator only on an event of probability tending to zero.  It follows that
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P)\}
 =J_\tau(P)\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)+o_P(1)
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}\right).
\]

The maps \(p\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T}\) and \(p\mapsto J_\tau(p)\) are continuous at \(P\).  Therefore, again ignoring an event whose probability tends to zero,
\[
 \widehat V_n
 =J_\tau(\widehat p_n)\widehat\Sigma_nJ_\tau(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}
 \xrightarrow{P}J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On the equality branch, the sound certificate procedure proves that \(\tau_y(P)=T_{D,y}(P)\) for every represented causal DAG \(D\); by the truncated-factorization definition this common value is the causal cell probability \(P_x(Y=y)\), not merely an observed regression.

Finally assume the declared nondegeneracy condition \(\sigma_y^2>0\).  The scalar marginal limit, variance consistency, and the cited Slutsky lemma imply
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The boundary points \(\pm1.96\) have zero standard-normal probability, so the coverage converges to
\[
 \Pr\{-1.96\leq Z\leq1.96\}=2\Phi(1.96)-1\approx0.950004,
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
This proves the corrected coverage claim and every other assertion.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(W_1,W_2,\ldots\) are independent and identically distributed random vectors in a fixed finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(\mathbb E W_1=0\), and \(\mathbb E\|W_1\|^2<\infty\), then \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i\) converges in distribution to the centered multivariate normal law with covariance \(\mathbb E(W_1W_1^{\mathsf T})\), allowing a singular covariance matrix.

attestation.note: The displayed finite-dimensional i.i.d. central limit theorem is the specialization used here; a stable book DOI is supplied.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(r_n(T_n-\theta)\) converges in distribution to \(T\), \(r_n\to\infty\), and \(g\) is differentiable at \(\theta\), then \(r_n\{g(T_n)-g(\theta)\}\) converges in distribution to \(Dg(\theta)T\).

attestation.note: The displayed differentiable-map limit is the theorem used here; the stable chapter DOI is supplied.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(X_n\) converges in distribution to \(X\) and \(Y_n\) converges in probability to a constant \(c\), then sums and products converge to the corresponding sum and product; if \(c\neq0\), then \(X_n/Y_n\) converges in distribution to \(X/c\).

attestation.note: The displayed scalar quotient form is the cited Slutsky lemma; a stable book DOI is supplied.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(R\) be a real closed field, let \(L\subseteq R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) be an ideal, and let \(f\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\).  The polynomial \(f\) vanishes at every point of the real variety of \(L\) if and only if there are an integer \(a\geq1\) and finitely many \(q_i\in R[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) such that \(f^{2a}+\sum_iq_i^2\in L\).

attestation.note: The displayed statement is the equality-only specialization of the cited Real Nullstellensatz; the stable DOI is supplied because no source transcription is embedded.

added_lemmas.statement: Every two real closed fields satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of ordered fields.  In particular, a first-order sentence with rational coefficients holds over \(\mathbb R\) if and only if it holds over the real algebraic closure of \(\mathbb Q\).

source.locator: Quantifier-elimination theorem for real closed fields

attestation.note: The displayed transfer consequence is the exact model-theoretic fact used; the stable publisher page is supplied.

added_lemmas.statement: For a finite family of SA-MPDAGs \(\mathfrak G=\{G_i\}\) and disjoint \(X,Y\), let \(A_i=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{G_i}(Y)\).  Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient criterion for simultaneous identification: each \(G_i\) has no proper semidirected path from \(X\) to \(Y\) beginning with an undirected edge, and for each pair \((G_i,G_j)\), either the relevant chain-component parent sets agree in both directions or the reweighted ancestral graphs \(\operatorname{RM}(G_i;X,Y)\) and \(\operatorname{RM}(G_j;X,Y)\) are Markov equivalent.

attestation.note: Paraphrased directly from the published theorem statement and its proof at the specified location.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Lemma (finite equality certificates).  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\), then there are finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) certifying that \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  If the extension and every polynomial and product in those identities are supplied in expanded exact form, with exponents in unary, deterministic exact verification is polynomial in the total expanded certificate length.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The real-radical and saturation definitions imply existence of finite identities, but no declared assumption or cited effective theorem establishes that their degree, coefficient height, and term count are all bounded by the particular quantity \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  A construction definition for \(c_0\) cannot itself prove that quantitative property.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Theorem 2 (sound partial certificate procedure).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the two output formats of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) are mutually exclusive and sound.  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and \(y\), the equality branch returns \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with finite identities and \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for all \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), \(D\), and \(y\).  If some normal form is nonzero, its bounded rational enumeration contains at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) candidate tables and returns a separator if and only if such a candidate of coordinate bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) exists; every returned separator certifies unequal graphwise intervention vectors.  Thus the equality branch implies a common intervention law, but unconditional termination of the nonzero branch and the converse from a common law to the equality branch are not asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: A nonzero normal form gives a real point of the saturated equality variety, not necessarily a strictly positive rational point satisfying every exact-oracle inequality.  Thus the frozen core proves soundness of both outputs and a finite conditional search, but not unconditional termination or the claimed if-and-only-if characterization.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference).  Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\).  Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.9500042097\ldots\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: With the literal cutoff \(1.96\), the standard-normal coverage is \(2\Phi(1.96)-1=0.9500042097\ldots\), not exactly \(0.95\).  All differentiability, Gaussian-limit, and covariance-consistency assertions remain unchanged.

proposed.statement: Lemma (finite equality certificates).  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\), then there are finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identities over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\) certifying that \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  If the extension and every polynomial and product in those identities are supplied in expanded exact form, with exponents in unary, deterministic exact verification is polynomial in the total expanded certificate length.
proposed.justification: A termination theorem is meaningful only when both branches carry finite, size-accounted certificates.
proposed.gap: Existing effective real-algebraic bounds do not instantiate the complete expanded certificate contract for these rational causal circuits.
proposed.consumer: Independent proof checkers can validate equality outputs without trusting the computer-algebra system that produced them.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim no longer uses the unproved quantitative certificate bound, so its dependency and free-symbol metadata must be updated atomically.

For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the two output formats of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) are mutually exclusive and sound.  If \(\operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and \(y\), the equality branch returns \(\tau=(T_{D_0,y})_y\) with finite identities and \(T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)\) for all \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), \(D\), and \(y\).  If some normal form is nonzero, its bounded rational enumeration contains at most \(2^{2m(B_{\mathrm{cert}}+1)}\) candidate tables and returns a separator if and only if such a candidate of coordinate bit length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) exists; every returned separator certifies unequal graphwise intervention vectors.  Thus the equality branch implies a common intervention law, but unconditional termination of the nonzero branch and the converse from a common law to the equality branch are not asserted.
proposed.justification: The theorem replaces arbitrary selection among tied sparsest graphs by an effect-complete common-functional-or-counterexample contract.
proposed.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo prove only a sufficient simultaneous criterion; Perkovic is complete for one MPDAG rather than a tied family across MECs.
proposed.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP all-ties output can report a common effect circuit or an exact ambiguity table instead of choosing one tied graph.

proposed.statement: For \(V=\{1,2,3,4\}\) with binary \(\{-1,+1\}\) states, the tuple \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\). The table \(p_{\star}\) has exactly the elementary CIs \(1\perp2\), \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\), \(3\perp4\), and \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\). Among all \(543\) labelled DAGs, exactly \(50\) are I-maps, and the unique four-edge minima are \(D_A\) and \(D_B\), which lie in distinct MECs. Their probabilities for \(Y_3=+1\) under \(do(Y_1=+1)\) are \(13/20\) and \(1/2\), respectively.
proposed.justification: The finite instance proves that the target family is nonvacuous beyond one Markov equivalence class.
proposed.gap: The examples in Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo motivate tied sparsest outputs but do not provide this binary rational exact-oracle enumeration certificate.
proposed.consumer: Implementers obtain a unit test whose graph counts, oracle bits, and intervention gap are all checkable by exact arithmetic.

proposed.statement: Corollary 1 (strictness relative to Teh--Sadeghi--Soo). For the certified input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) and query \(P_{Y_1=+1}(Y_3=+1)\), the sufficient graphical conditions of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo are not satisfied, whereas \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns a rational positive separator; the table \(p_{\star}\) is an explicit admissible separator with graphwise values \(13/20\) under \(D_A\) and \(1/2\) under \(D_B\). Hence SparseSIM-ID strictly tightens that sufficient-only test on certified tied-sparsest inputs by resolving at least one query on which it is undecided.
proposed.justification: This finite corollary turns the comparator relation into an auditable strict inclusion rather than a prose promise.
proposed.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient graphical criterion and leave necessity unresolved; this certified exact-oracle instance is outside their decided region but receives a checkable nonidentification certificate.
proposed.consumer: A regression test for Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP can verify that an undecided graphical case is reported as exact ambiguity rather than silently selecting a graph.

proposed.statement: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference).  Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\).  Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.9500042097\ldots\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).
proposed.justification: A certified population functional should produce standard sampling inference without graphwise duplicate estimates.
proposed.gap: Chang, Guo, and Malinsky handle data-driven graph selection by interval unions; this theorem instead gives pointwise plug-in inference for one fixed certified oracle, tied family, and arithmetic circuit.
proposed.consumer: After a population or externally certified discovery analysis, practitioners can estimate the common intervention probability with one covariance calculation.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Show that every intervention signature outside \(K_{\mathcal I}\) is nonzero at a strictly positive rational table satisfying all bit-one equalities and all bit-zero inequalities, with coordinate height at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Real-radical nonmembership only exposes a real point on some saturated equality component.  Saturation excludes zero cells and denominators algebraically but does not choose the positive sign chamber, enforce the exact-oracle nonvanishing blocks, or provide rational points.  The supplied rational feasibility witness may lie on a different component on which the signature vanishes.
open_obligations.attempted: The common-law reduction, the real-radical evaluation argument, and rational approximation were checked.  Approximation cannot preserve conditional-independence equations exactly, and the minimum-edge certificate adds no equations.  Rational DAG or forest charts close the step only when an effect-separating chart is already known.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct an effect-separating finite rational atlas for every accepted exact oracle and prove both the advertised global height bound and the bounded-treewidth singly exponential refinement.
open_obligations.obstruction: No frozen hypothesis makes all relevant conditional-independence components rational or proves that DAG and directed-forest charts meet every component detected by an intervention signature.  Bounded treewidth controls graph decompositions but, by itself, does not control rational parametrizability or arithmetic height.
open_obligations.attempted: Clearing denominators on a single rational chart and searching a Cartesian rational grid works, and the four-node instance supplies one explicit rational curve.  Extending this chartwise argument fails exactly at the unproved coverage or effect-separation step.
open_obligations.partial_result: One computable conditional result holds.  Let \(\phi:U\to\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) be a rational map defined over \(\mathbb Q\) on a nonempty open box \(U=\prod_{j=1}^k(a_j,b_j)\) with rational endpoints, and suppose all denominators of \(\phi\) are nonzero on \(U\).  If \(F_{D,y}\circ\phi=N/Q\) in reduced form with \(N\in\mathbb Q[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) nonzero and total degree \(e\), choose \(e+1\) distinct rational numbers in each interval \((a_j,b_j)\).  A nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(e\) cannot vanish on the entire Cartesian grid: induction on \(k\), using the univariate root bound for the last coordinate, proves this assertion.  Thus at most \((e+1)^k\) grid evaluations produce a rational \(t\in U\) with \(N(t)\neq0\), and \(p^\dagger=\phi(t)\) is a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator.  What remains unproved is that the recursively oriented DAG or forest charts cover every nonzero intervention signature, any uniform comparison of the resulting grid heights with \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), and any singly exponential bound from bounded treewidth.
